slides.title: Platform margin gained eleven points, all of it after the 2022 repricing
slides.subtitle: Gross margin, platform product line, 2021-24

points.lead: Repricing did most of the work
points.text: the December 2022 list revision lifted realised price 6% and cost nothing to deliver.
unit infrastructure cost dropped 22% as the 2023 migration finished.
tickets per account held at 1.4 a month while accounts grew 38%.

slides.title: Three conditions decide the FY25 plan; one is inside our control
slides.subtitle: Sensitivities on the FY25 margin plan

points.text: Two competitors repriced down in Q3. A matching cut costs 4.1pp of FY25 margin and is the single largest exposure on the plan.

points.lead: The cloud contract renews at terms
points.text: The current agreement expires in March. The committed-spend discount is worth 2.6pp and the renewal has not been negotiated.
Enterprise carries 9pp more margin than mid-market. The shift added 1.8pp last year and depends on a pipeline we do control.

slides.title: The 2022 repricing changed the trend, not just the level
slides.subtitle: Gross margin, platform product line, 2021-24

points.text: List prices rose 6% in December 2022, the first revision in four years, applied at renewal so no account saw a mid-term increase.
Realised price followed within two quarters and has held. Churn ran at 4.1% against 3.8%, inside the band the pricing committee accepted.
Volume growth was unchanged either side, so the gain is price, not mix. The 2024 points come from infrastructure cost, and that source is nearly spent.

slides.source: Pricing committee minutes; finance close, FY24

slides.title: Four teams cut cycle time; the two that did not share one constraint
slides.subtitle: Median cycle time by team, days, Q1 vs Q4 2024

points.text: Payments, Identity, Billing and Search each cut four days or more, and all four had adopted trunk-based release by February.
Ledger and Reporting are the only teams still releasing behind a monthly change board, and both are flat within noise.

points.lead: The constraint is the board, not the team
points.text: Ledger runs the same practices as Payments on every other measure, which leaves the release gate as the difference that matters.

slides.subtitle: Options assessed against the FY26 volume forecast

points.text: 18k units a month, live in eleven weeks, and it needs 60 operators in a market where we filled 19 of 40 roles last year.
44k units a month and the lowest unit cost of the three, but $12m of capital and nothing before Q3 FY26.
31k units a month at a 23% cost premium, available in six weeks, and it puts the quality system outside our audit boundary.
